about.title: About the Program
about.subtitle: Cultivating forward-looking talent in Agentic AI and Physical AI in response to the AI paradigm shift

origin.title: Program Background
origin.intro: In recent years, AI technology has advanced rapidly, with continual breakthroughs in model capabilities and simulation results. Yet most AI education and training still remains at the stage of "using models" and "idealized simulation." It is often only when AI systems truly enter real life and industrial settings that we discover the challenges are just beginning.
origin.realityGapTitle: The Real-World Gap in Physical Systems
origin.realityGapBody: Tasks that run smoothly in a simulated environment, once connected to physical hardware, must contend with motor error, sensor noise, response latency, and environmental uncertainty.
origin.dynamicBody: In everyday life, problems are often multifaceted and constantly changing, requiring simultaneous consideration of user needs, situational judgment, and resource constraints rather than being solved by a single command.
origin.insight1: Many applied AI systems are not simply "answering questions"; they must start from the user's perspective—understanding needs, breaking down tasks, and continually adjusting their course of action.
origin.insight2: This shows that what current agent development lacks is often not model capability, but rather experience drawn from real usage scenarios and the ability to integrate systems.
origin.positioning: Therefore, NAPAI focuses its AI talent cultivation on two forward-looking pillars: Agentic AI and Physical AI:
origin.pillar1: Cultivating agentic capabilities that can proactively reason, plan, and respond to user needs
origin.pillar2: Cultivating hands-on skills to implement AI in physical systems under real-world constraints
origin.closing: By integrating these two pillars, NAPAI is committed to cultivating forward-looking AI talent who can bridge the gap between models, simulation, and the real world to genuinely solve real-world problems.
origin.banner: The next step for AI is not just stronger models, but systems that understand real needs and act in the real world.

goals.title: Program Goals
goals.intro: NAPAI adopts a "lean but focused, results-driven" strategy, targeting two core technical pillars and integrating seed-teacher training, co-creation of course modules, pilot demonstration courses, student hands-on competitions, and community building.
goals.feature1Body: Co-edited course maps and a GitHub course repository
goals.feature2Body: Cultivating AI professionals with cross-domain hands-on skills
goals.feature3Body: Enhancing teachers' instructional and practical capabilities
goals.closing: Through hands-on projects and competitions, students are guided to focus on real industry scenarios and societal needs, laying a solid talent foundation for the future development of Taiwan's AI industry and intelligent applications.

faq.subtitle: Frequently asked questions about the study groups and curriculum program
faq.moreText: Feel free to reach out anytime—we're happy to help.

q1.question: Who can serve as a core seed teacher for the study groups?
q1.answer: Teachers who have conducted research in robotics or Agentic AI, or who have previously taught courses related to robotics or Agentic AI.

q2.question: Who can take part in the study groups?
q2.answer: Teachers interested in teaching or building with Agentic AI and Physical AI, along with their graduate students, and teachers willing to participate in course module development. Each seed teacher may bring 1–2 teaching assistants to the study group.

q3.question: Study group schedule
q3.answer: In the first phase, course modules are developed mainly through biweekly study groups (6 sessions in total). In the second phase, the developed courses are pilot-taught in workshops and revised based on the pilot results, while an open-source courseware platform is built.

q4.question: Expected outcomes of the study groups
q4.answer: Complete the open-source courseware platform and update and maintain it regularly.
